subject: spanish
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA GCSE Spanish specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Context 1: Identity, Lifestyle and Culture
units.blurb: Students' lives, families, interests and culture in Spanish-speaking communities

units.name: Context 2: Local, National, International and Global Areas of Interest
units.blurb: Local area, social and global issues, travel and tourism

units.name: Context 3: School Life, Studies and the World of Work
units.blurb: Education, jobs and future plans at home and in Spanish-speaking communities

units.name: Skills: Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing
units.blurb: The four assessed language skills applied across all three contexts

topics.name: Myself, My Family, Relationships and Choices
topics.blurb: Describing yourself, family and friends, and the relationships and choices in your life

topics.name: Social Media and New Technology
topics.blurb: Online communications, computers, tablets and smartphones

topics.name: Free Time, Leisure and Daily Routine
topics.blurb: Sport, hobbies, cinema, TV, music, fashion, eating out, shopping and daily routine

topics.name: Culture, Customs, Festivals and Celebrations
topics.blurb: Festivals, national holidays, cultural events, celebrations and cuisine

topics.name: My Local Area and the Wider Environment
topics.blurb: Home, neighbourhood, town or city, places to visit, region and country

topics.name: Community Involvement
topics.blurb: Charity and voluntary work in your community

topics.name: Social and Global Issues
topics.blurb: Health, lifestyle, anti-social behaviour, caring for others and the environment

topics.name: Travel and Tourism
topics.blurb: Holidays, destinations, transport, weather, accommodation and activities

topics.name: My Studies and School Life
topics.blurb: School subjects, uniform, timetable, rules and regulations

topics.name: Extra-Curricular Activities
topics.blurb: Clubs, societies, events, trips and visits

topics.name: Part-Time Jobs and Money Management
topics.blurb: Evening and weekend work, work experience and managing money

topics.name: Future Plans and Career
topics.blurb: Post-16 education, further study, employment, aspirations and choices

topics.name: Listening
topics.blurb: Understanding spoken language, identifying key points, details and opinions, and deducing meaning

topics.name: Speaking
topics.blurb: Communicating and interacting in conversation, responding spontaneously with accurate pronunciation

topics.name: Reading
topics.blurb: Understanding written texts, identifying main points and details, and deducing meaning

topics.name: Writing
topics.blurb: Producing accurate written language, manipulating vocabulary and grammar for different purposes

connections.why: Talking about family and friends naturally extends into describing the leisure and daily routines shared with them
Vocabulary for social media and technology supports discussion of social issues such as online behaviour and well-being
Leisure and free-time language reappears when describing holiday activities, eating out and shopping while travelling
Knowledge of customs and festivals enriches talk about destinations and cultural experiences abroad
Describing your home and daily routine builds the place vocabulary needed to discuss your wider local area and environment
Knowing your local area is the springboard for discussing environmental and social issues that affect it
Charity and voluntary work is a practical response to the social and global issues studied alongside it
Talking about current studies leads directly into discussing post-16 education and career plans
Part-time work and money management feed into aspirations and choices about future employment
School life and extra-curricular activities together describe a full picture of a student's time at school
Familiar personal topics like family and interests are core prompts for the speaking conversation tasks
Everyday leisure vocabulary gives students accessible content for written tasks on daily life
Travel and tourism scenarios are common contexts for listening passages and authentic spoken material
Social and global issues feature in the longer reading texts where students extract detail and opinion
Future plans and aspirations are frequent prompts for extended written responses and opinions
School life is a familiar context for spontaneous conversation and exchanging opinions in speaking
Understanding spoken Spanish accurately is the foundation for responding and interacting in conversation
Reading models of written Spanish supplies the vocabulary and structures students reuse in their own writing
